stem: Researchers are studying the processing and intracellular transport of mRNA in cultured human fibroblasts.  Newly synthesized RNA is labeled and tracked as it undergoes maturation, translation, and degradation.  Which of the following events involving mRNA occurs exclusively in the cytoplasm?​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​

options.label: D
options.text: Multiple adenine nucleotide attachment to the 3′ end

explanation:
Precursor mRNA (pre-mRNA) undergoes processing in the nucleus before export to the cytoplasm.  These modifications, many of which occur during transcription, include:

  • 5′ capping:  A 7-methylguanosine residue is attached to the 5′ end through a unique 5′–5′ triphosphate linkage.  This cap protects mRNA from exonuclease degradation and supports nuclear export and translation (Choice A).

  • Poly(A) tail addition:  Cleavage and polyadenylation factors recognize the polyadenylation signal (typically AAUAAA) and cleave the transcript downstream of this signal.  Polyadenylate polymerase then adds adenine nucleotides to the new 3′ end to form a poly(A) tail, which helps stabilize mRNA (Choice D).

  • Splicing:  The spliceosome, composed of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) and additional proteins, removes introns and joins the remaining exons.  Exons are retained in mature mRNA and include both protein-coding sequences and untranslated regions (Choices C and E).

Mature mRNA is exported to the cytoplasm, where it can associate with ribosomes for translation.  Some mRNAs that are not actively being translated instead associate with processing bodies (P bodies), which are cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules involved in translational repression and regulation of mRNA decay (via decapping enzymes, exonucleases).  P bodies can also store transcripts and later release them for translation (mRNA storage).

Educational objective:Pre-mRNA undergoes nuclear processing, including 5′ capping, poly(A) tail addition, and splicing, before export.  Cytoplasmic processing bodies (P bodies) contain translationally repressed mRNAs and proteins involved in mRNA decay.  They can also store mRNAs that are subsequently released for translation.​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​
